pr_body:
This change invokes `Engine#maybeRefresh()` when a shard is search-idle and becomes search-active in `IndexShard#ensureShardSearchActive(...)` (used to be named `waitShardSearchActive(...)`).

Prior to this change shard level search execution is idle until the schedule refresh has been execute. This includes the time it takes for the refresh to be scheduled (which is a full second). This unnecessarily increases the query time of a search request.

Closes #95544
pr_title: Trigger refresh when shard becomes search active
pr_comment: (accidentally pushed 'ready for review' on this PR... too many open browser tabs)

review_comment: Because `makeShardSearchActive(...)` now triggers a refresh, we can no longer invoke this method many times without a refresh to happen. Before this was possible in this test and then just invoke `scheduleRefresh(...)` and all the listeners were invoked.
In particular, `addRefreshListener` might have performed the refresh already in edge cases.
Can we assert that we are not on a transport thread here (or that we are on a search or refresh thread)? Also, probably worth checking in more detail by checking callers (did not do so).

Quickly looking this method is used by get, mget, explain and term vector transport actions too. So I guess we need to allow this method for these apis as well. Hopefully these api don't call this method from transport thread...
Looks like `TransportOpenPointInTimeAction` calls this method from a transport thread.

Unfortunately the `ensureShardSearchActive(...)` method (before `awaitShardSearchActive(...)`) is called in more places from transport_worker thread.

After adding the assertion we talked about, this assertion tripped in many places. For example in the `SearchService#executeQueryPhase(...)` case:

if (location == pendingRefreshLocation.get()) {
